How to protect yourself from phishing with mobile network security
sum: Why do we click on links even when we know the cybersecurity risks?

A link that arrives via WhatsApp. An alarming SMS from the bank. A QR code in a restaurant. A Microsoft Teams notification. An urgent email. A document someone shares while we are on the metro. A message from the boss just before going into a meeting.
We click without hesitating, without thinking, because that is how life works today: fast-paced, with multiple fronts to deal with and fires to put out at any given moment…
And yet, we have been on our guard for some time, with a constant warning in the back of our minds: do not open it, do not download it, check the sender, look carefully at the URL, be suspicious.
We make mistakes when we are in a hurry, which is quite often, when we are tired, when something looks convincing enough or simply when we are thinking about something else and let our guard down.

Our own cybersecurity requires training, common sense and good habits. That is not going to change. But I think we are asking too much if we expect people to be able to distinguish between a potential scam and something legitimate all day long, at every moment and in every situation.

Even more so now, when artificial intelligence is doing extraordinary things for all of us, but can also be used for less positive purposes, such as trying to deceive us. A phishing email no longer has to be full of spelling mistakes. It can be well written, tailored to the recipient’s context and sound entirely plausible.

Digital euro mandate puts Telefonica stock in focus
sum: Telefónica and Minsait have been selected as one of two successful tenderers to deploy communications and security infrastructure for a future digital euro. The announcement was published on Monday, November 2, 2026, and was reported by WebWire.

The consortium will connect the European Central Bank ecosystem with private and public payment facilitators, banks, fintech companies and payment service providers. Telefónica will contribute communications infrastructure through Telefónica Global Solutions and Telefónica Tech, while Minsait will provide application integration, digital identity, trust services and cybersecurity capabilities.

The planned infrastructure combines an MPLS network, SD-WAN capabilities and cybersecurity services. These systems are intended to connect different locations securely and support the exchange of information between the participants in the future digital euro ecosystem. Minsait will add API-based integration, certificates, access controls, encryption and security monitoring.

The contract is scheduled to enter into force on May 3, 2027, and runs for 10 years. The project is designed to support a digital means of payment that would complement cash across the euro area. The announcement does not disclose financial terms for Telefónica, so the immediate investment relevance lies in the company's positioning in critical communications, cloud and cybersecurity infrastructure rather than in a quantified earnings contribution.

Telefónica's next scheduled corporate milestone is the publication of its January-September 2026 results on Thursday, November 12, according to the company's shareholder and investor calendar. That report will give investors a broader basis for assessing operating trends, cash generation and the contribution potential of business-to-business technology activities.

Lula Victory Triggers Selloff in Brazilian and European Stocks
sum: Investors sold Brazilian and European equities after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated Flávio Bolsonaro in Brazil's presidential runoff on Sunday, October 25, 2026, reversing expectations of a more business-friendly government and intensifying concerns about public debt and fiscal discipline.

Brazil's Superior Electoral Court reported that Lula won 51.8% of valid votes, compared with Bolsonaro's 48.2%, with nearly all ballots counted. The result marked the first time since Brazil returned to direct elections in 1989 that a candidate won the runoff after losing the first round.

The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF fell more than 27% in premarket trading on Monday, October 26, according to reports by CNBC and Yahoo Finance. The decline put the fund on track for its steepest single-day loss since at least 2000.

Brazilian companies listed in the United States also suffered sharp losses. CNBC reported that Petrobras fell 24% in premarket trading, Itaú Unibanco dropped 26%, Ambev declined 13%, Vale lost 3.3%, and Embraer slipped 2.6%.

The selloff spread to European companies with significant Brazilian operations. Shares of Spain's Banco Santander fell nearly 4% and telecommunications group Telefónica dropped 7.2% in early trading, while AB InBev declined 3.5%, according to Yahoo Finance. Spain's IBEX 35 fell 0.3% and Portugal's PSI 20 lost 0.7%, despite gains across other European indexes.

Investors had favored Bolsonaro because his campaign promised fiscal consolidation, privatization and business-oriented reforms. His lead after the first round had reinforced expectations of a more market-friendly outcome, making Lula's victory an unexpected shock.
RBC Capital Markets analyst Benjamin Toms linked the market reaction to concerns about Lula's approach to public finances.

Cloud, Security, and Regulatory Compliance: The Technical Challenges Shaping the Evolution of the Cloud
sum: The evolution of the cloud is driven by the combination of infrastructure, security, data, artificial intelligence, and regulatory compliance to address new technological challenges.
What technical challenges are driving the evolution of cloud environments?

Cloud technologies enable the deployment and management of infrastructure that is more flexible, scalable, and tailored to the needs of each organization. Cloud technology plays a very important role among digital technologies.

Currently, cloud projects combine public, private, and hybrid environments with security, data, and artificial intelligence capabilities. This approach allows organizations to address increasingly complex technological needs from an integrated perspective.

In this context, the cloud is establishing itself as one of the key technologies for moving toward digital infrastructures that are more flexible, secure, and ready to incorporate new capabilities. Its evolution, along with fields such as artificial intelligence, data, and cybersecurity, contributes to the development of more advanced technology services and reinforces Telefónica’s role as a gateway to digital technologies, while also fostering a more innovative and competitive company.
What technical capabilities does the cloud offer public and private organizations today?
- Integration of security, data, and artificial intelligence capabilities.

AT&T is selling AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2 billion in cash, leaving the country after more than a decade.
The Mexican mobile market is going to look a lot different next year after AT&T and Telefónica complete the sales of their respective businesses in the country.

AT&T agreed to sell its operation, AT&T Mexico, to a consortium comprising local cable and broadcast company Grupo Televisa and investment firm Fintech Holdings for $2 billion in cash. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.
Shedding the Mexican business after more than ten years in the market will allow AT&T to focus capital investment on building out fiber and 5G connectivity in the US, according to the carrier.

The deal follows Telefónica's long-awaited sale of Movistar in Mexico, announced in April. The Spanish operator is selling its Mexican business for $450 million to a consortium led by telecom-as-a-service platform provider Oxio and Newfoundland Capital Management. The transaction reportedly cleared a regulatory hurdle early this month with approval from Mexico's National Antitrust Commission but has not yet been finalized, according to El Economista.

SpaceX spectrum deal to expand its Starlink network in the US sends telecom stocks tumbling
sum: SpaceX is muscling in on US telecom territory and it's rattling the shares of top US communications giants on Friday.

SpaceX jumped as much as 4%, riding a wave of bullishness following an announcement on Thursday that the company had reached a deal to acquire the nationwide rights to a block of low frequency airwaves, a development Musk described as a "very big deal" in a post on X.

"This prime low-band spectrum addresses one of the key remaining technical gaps that will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US," SpaceX stated in its announcement.

The company said that once it receives regulatory approval, it plans to deploy a hybrid network combining its satellite and ground technology that will allow it to significantly scale device connectivity. This comes as global reliance on Starlink has grown significantly in recent years.
The news that SpaceX could expand its network to more US users sent shares of major telecom companies tumbling.
Germany's Deutsche Telekom, the majority owner of T-Mobile, and Spain's Telefónica were down 8% and 4.5% respectively in European trading.

Wall Street analysts see the deal as a major step forward for SpaceX as the company maneuvers to become the dominant satellite connectivity provider, building what it describes as "the world's most advanced mobile network."

Abenójar Tungsten, a Spanish tungsten and gold mine, to list in London
sum: Abenójar Tungsten, a company promoting the development of the El Moto Mine in Ciudad Real to extract tungsten and gold starting in 2029, has launched its listing on the London Stock Exchange to finance its 211-million-euro project by announcing to the market its ‘intention’ to execute an offering of part of its shares on that exchange to begin trading in the coming weeks.

The banks Peel Hunt, BMO, Deutsche Bank, and Canaccord will handle the placement, which could amount to several tens of millions of euros and through which Abenójar aims to enter the main market of the London Stock Exchange.

The funds will be used to finance the construction of the mine (estimated investment of 211 million) and to pay part of the agreed price upon acquiring the operation. Alongside the capital that may be raised in the offering, Deutsche Bank will provide bank financing of up to 120 million euros.

Movistar Estudiantes Officially Unveils the 2026-2027 Season
sum: The official presentation of Movistar Estudiantes’ 2026-27 season brought together players, coaching staff, academy teams, sponsors, institutions, media representatives and fans this Monday at the Espacio Movistar in the Telefónica Building. Held on Madrid’s Gran Vía, the event marked the start of a new chapter for the club, shaped by a new institutional era and a message that will accompany the team throughout the season: Indestructibles.

Hosted by José Ajero and Iyi Martín, the presentation began by looking back at the club’s recent history. One of the highlights of the event was a tribute to Jayson Granger following his retirement from professional basketball. The Uruguayan player arrived at Ramiro at the age of 15, developed through the club’s academy and made his ACB debut wearing the Estu jersey before going on to enjoy a long and successful national and international career. Movistar Estudiantes honoured his legacy and connection with the club with a special video and his appearance on stage.

The event also paid tribute to those who have led the club in recent years. Ignacio Triana and Vicente Olivenza, Movistar Estudiantes’ principal shareholders during the past seasons, were recognised for their commitment to and involvement with the club.

The presentation then moved on to the unveiling of a new institutional phase for Movistar Estudiantes, led by its new majority shareholder, Diego Megía, who addressed attendees to share the vision for this new chapter while highlighting the club’s identity and values.

On the court, three senior teams will take centre stage this season. The Women in Black begin a new Liga Femenina Endesa campaign under head coach Isaac Fernández; the men’s first team, guided by Toni Ten, prepares for another season with ambition and determination; and the men’s reserve team embarks on a historic journey with its debut in Segunda FEB following promotion last season. Captains and coaches from all three teams also took to the stage to share their goals and expectations ahead of the new campaign.

Telefónica (BME:TEF) Is Back In The Spotlight, What Is Driving Attention?
sum: Telefónica (BME:TEF) drew fresh attention after its latest share price closed at €3.75, with recent returns mixed between the past week, month, past 3 months and year.

Recent trading has tilted in Telefónica's favour, with the latest move taking the share price to €3.75 and a 7.79% year to date share price return. However, the 1 year total shareholder return declined 11.5%, which suggests short term momentum is picking up while longer term holders have had a tougher run.
Scan Telefónica alongside other potential rebound stories by checking our curated list of 169 high quality undervalued stocks that combine solid fundamentals with room for sentiment to shift.

Telefónica has edged higher in the short term, while longer term investors are still in the red. Does that recent shift leave more upside for new buyers, or is most of the easy risk reward already gone as valuation comes into focus?

Against Telefónica's last close at €3.75, the most followed narrative pegs fair value at about €3.96, which implies a modest discount and puts the focus squarely on how the business reshapes its portfolio and cash generation over time.

The completion of large-scale portfolio optimization and monetization of non-core assets (sale of Argentina, Peru, Colombia, Uruguay, Ecuador, etc.) is reducing geographic risk and freeing up significant capital (€3 billion+). The strategy to focus on core markets (Spain, Brazil, Germany, UK) enables redeployment of resources to what are viewed as higher-return areas, with an emphasis on free cash flow and ROCE.
Still, Telefónica carries high leverage and faces pressure in mature markets like Spain and Germany. This could undermine the current undervalued narrative if progress stalls.

Telefónica to Share How Risk-Based Aftersales Planning Protects Mission-Critical Service Levels
sum: At LogiAftersales 2026, Telefónica will share practical insights on balancing service availability, and inventory investment across complex spare parts networks

BOSTON, MA, UNITED STATES, September 17, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- ToolsGroup today announced that Telefónica SA will share how risk-based aftersales planning can help global service organizations protect mission-critical availability without tying up unnecessary capital in spare parts inventory. The session will feature Michel Hasenclever, Head Global Supply Planning at Telefónica SA, and will focus on practical ways to reduce service-level risk across complex, multi-echelon service networks.

Aftersales organizations are facing a sharper planning challenge as intermittent demand and long-tail SKU portfolios collide with global supply disruptions and rising service expectations, making spare parts inventory decisions more complex than ever.A single missing part can affect availability, service commitments, and customer trust, while excess inventory can constrain working capital and add operational cost.

In his session, Hasenclever will discuss how organizations can use probabilistic planning, multi-echelon inventory optimization (MEIO), and data-driven inventory policies to make more resilient decisions across distributed service networks. The discussion will highlight how risk-aware planning helps teams move beyond averages, quantify service trade-offs, and align inventory strategies with both customer commitments and business performance.

“In aftersales, every inventory decision is a service decision,” said Hasenclever. “When demand is intermittent and networks are complex, planning based on averages is no longer enough. Organizations need to understand the probability of risk, the business impact of stockouts, and the value of each inventory investment so they can protect availability where it matters most.”

“Telefónica’s perspective reflects a broader shift in supply chain planning: companies need to understand risk, not just forecast demand,” said Sean Elliott, CEO of ToolsGroup. “In volatile environments, better outcomes come from better decisions. Organizations need planning systems that continuously evaluate trade-offs, adapt as conditions change, and help teams act with confidence.”
